# `silk/time/text_http`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The date and time format of HTTP header fields such as `Date`, `Last-Modified`, and `Expires`.

## When to use

Use [`HttpDate.write`](#HttpDate.impl.write) for a header field that a program sends and [`HttpDate.parse`](#HttpDate.impl.parse) for one
that it receives. For timestamps in other protocols and in files, use `Instant.parse` and
`Instant.writeUtc`, which read and write RFC 3339.

## Details

[`HttpDate.write`](#HttpDate.impl.write) writes the one form that RFC 9110 allows a sender, which is always 29 bytes:
`Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT`.

[`HttpDate.parse`](#HttpDate.impl.parse) reads the three forms that RFC 9110 requires of a recipient:

- `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT`
- `Sunday, 06-Nov-94 08:49:37 GMT`, where the years `70` to `99` are 1970 to 1999 and the
  years `00` to `69` are 2000 to 2069
- `Sun Nov  6 08:49:37 1994`

Names are case-sensitive. The name of the day must be a real day name, and the parser does not
check that it is the day of the date. Second `60` reads as `59`.

## Examples

### Write and read a header value

```silk
import silk.collections.slice { Slice }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.time.instant { Instant }
import silk.time.text { TimeParseError }
import silk.time.text_http { HttpDate }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut text: [u8; 29] = [0; 29]
  let length = HttpDate.write(Instant.fromUnixSeconds(784111777), &mut text, 0)
  // `text` is now `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT`.
  match HttpDate.parseBytes(Slice.view<u8>(&text, 0, length)) {
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Success { value } => {
      if value.unixSeconds() == 784111777 {
        return 0
      }
      return 1
    }
    Result<Instant, TimeParseError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 2
    }
  }
}
```

<a id="HttpDate.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub fn write(instant: Instant, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes `instant` as `Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT` at `output[at]` and returns `at + 29`.

#### Details

The format has whole seconds, so a fraction of a second is dropped. The year of `instant` in
UTC must be from 0 to 9999, or the function traps.

<a id="HttpDate.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Reads an instant from the value of an HTTP date header field, in any of the three forms of
RFC 9110.

#### Errors
- `UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `text` is not in one of the three forms.
- `OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist, such as `30 Feb` or hour `24`.

<a id="HttpDate.impl.parseBytes"></a>

### Associated function `parseBytes`

```silk
pub fn parseBytes(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Instant, TimeParseError>
```

Reads an instant from the bytes of the value of an HTTP date header field, in any of the
three forms of RFC 9110.

#### Errors
- `UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if `bytes` is not in one of the three forms.
- `OutOfRange` if the date or the time does not exist, such as `30 Feb` or hour `24`.
